claims.text: An environment variable is a name-value pair the operating system hands to a process when that process starts, so the run can read the value without opening a file.
claims.source_hint: POSIX.1 Base Definitions, ch. 8 Environment Variables; execve environ argument

claims.text: A new process receives its own copy of the environment at the moment it starts; the copy is made once and nothing added to the starter's set afterwards appears in it.
claims.source_hint: POSIX.1 System Interfaces, exec family: the new process image receives a copy of environ

claims.text: A process started by another begins with a copy of that other process's environment, unless the starter hands it a different set — which is exactly what `env NAME=value command` does.
claims.source_hint: POSIX.1 System Interfaces, fork/exec: environment inheritance; observed at stage-0 in outputs/stage-0/scripts/computer/env-demo.txt line 2

claims.text: A change a process makes to its own environment does not change the environment of the process that started it, and the changed copy does not persist after that process ends.
claims.source_hint: POSIX.1 System Interfaces, setenv/putenv: the change affects only the calling process image; .NET API reference, Environment.SetEnvironmentVariable(String, String), Remarks

claims.text: Setting a variable in one terminal does not reach a process that is already running, nor another terminal, because each of those already holds a copy made earlier.
claims.source_hint: .NET API reference, Environment.SetEnvironmentVariable, Remarks: a User/Machine write is inherited by new processes only

claims.text: Configuration usually arrives in three ways: files the program reads, the name-value pairs it starts with, and the words typed after the program's name. These are three of the usual ways, not a closed list.
claims.source_hint: POSIX.1 ch. 8 Environment Variables; execve argv and environ

claims.text: Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable(name) returns null when the name has no value in the current process's environment.
claims.source_hint: .NET API reference, System.Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable(String), Returns section

claims.text: The ?? operator yields its left operand when that operand is not null, and evaluates its right operand only otherwise, which is how the sample reaches for the address written into the file only when nothing was handed in.
claims.source_hint: C# language reference, ?? and ??= operators

claims.text: Environment.SetEnvironmentVariable(name, value) called with no target changes only the current process's environment, and a later GetEnvironmentVariable in the same run returns the new value.
claims.source_hint: .NET API reference, System.Environment.SetEnvironmentVariable(String, String), Remarks
